q: Which U.S. president proclaimed Thanksgiving a national holiday in 1863?
fact: Lincoln set it for the last Thursday of November, in the middle of the Civil War, after years of letters from magazine editor Sarah Josepha Hale.

q: In Friends' "The One with All the Thanksgivings," what does Monica put on her head to cheer up Chandler?
fact: She adds a fez and big sunglasses. Chandler tells her "I love you" for the first time.

q: The 1621 harvest feast at Plymouth was shared by the Pilgrims and which Native nation?
fact: Colonist Edward Winslow wrote that about 90 Wampanoag men came with their leader, Massasoit.

q: Which NFL team has hosted a Thanksgiving Day game nearly every year since 1934?
fact: The only break came during World War II (1939–1944). The Dallas Cowboys joined the tradition in 1966.

q: What is the name of the global day of charitable giving held right after Thanksgiving weekend?
fact: GivingTuesday started in 2012 at New York's 92nd Street Y and is now celebrated around the world.

q: Who traditionally arrives at the very end of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade?
fact: Santa's arrival kicks off the holiday season. The first parade, in 1924, was even called the Macy's Christmas Parade.

q: Which food is NOT part of the Thanksgiving meal Snoopy serves in A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving?
fact: Snoopy and Woodstock make toast, pretzel sticks, popcorn and jelly beans after Peppermint Patty invites herself over.

q: A baby turkey is called a…
fact: Adult males are toms (or gobblers), adult females are hens, and young males are jakes.

q: Which state produces the most cranberries in the U.S.?
fact: Wisconsin grows more than half the nation's cranberries. Ripe cranberries have air pockets, which is why they float when bogs are flooded for harvest.

q: Which state raises the most turkeys in the U.S.?
fact: Minnesota has led the nation for years, with North Carolina and Arkansas close behind.

q: Green bean casserole was invented in 1955 in which company's test kitchen?
fact: Home economist Dorcas Reilly created it with cream of mushroom soup and crispy fried onions. Her original recipe card is in the National Inventors Hall of Fame.

q: In Friends, Rachel's Thanksgiving trifle goes wrong because the cookbook pages stuck together. What ends up in it?
options: Beef sautéed with peas and onions
fact: Half the recipe was shepherd's pie. Joey loved it: "Custard, good. Jam, good. Meat, good!"

q: In 1939, FDR moved Thanksgiving a week earlier to lengthen the holiday shopping season. What did critics call it?
fact: The change was so unpopular that Congress fixed Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November in 1941.

q: What did broadcaster John Madden famously hand out to standout players on Thanksgiving?
fact: Madden also helped popularize the turducken, a chicken stuffed inside a duck stuffed inside a turkey.

q: Which classic film opens at the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, where Kris Kringle replaces a drunk Santa?
fact: The 1947 film was shot during the real parade, and Edmund Gwenn won an Oscar for playing Kris.

q: When does Canada celebrate Thanksgiving?
fact: Canada fixed the date in 1957. Its earlier harvest season is one reason it comes first.

q: Turkey often gets blamed for post-feast sleepiness because it contains which amino acid?
fact: Turkey has about as much tryptophan as chicken. A huge, carb-heavy meal is the bigger reason everyone dozes off.

q: Most "yams" sold in U.S. grocery stores are actually…
fact: True yams are a different plant from Africa and Asia. Producers labeled soft orange sweet potatoes "yams" to set them apart.

q: Which president made the White House turkey pardon an official annual tradition in 1989?
fact: Earlier presidents sometimes spared a turkey, but Bush made the formal pardon a yearly event.

q: In a 1784 letter to his daughter, which Founding Father called the turkey "a much more respectable bird" than the bald eagle?
fact: Franklin never formally proposed the turkey as the national bird. He was poking fun at the eagle design on a society's badge.

q: "Over the River and Through the Wood" started as an 1844 poem about traveling to grandfather's house for which holiday?
fact: Lydia Maria Child wrote it as "The New-England Boy's Song about Thanksgiving Day." Many people now sing it at Christmas.

q: What is the anatomical name for a turkey's wishbone?
fact: The furcula forms when two collarbones fuse, and it acts like a spring when birds flap their wings.

q: What was the first character balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, in 1927?
fact: Balloons replaced the live Central Park Zoo animals that marched in the first parades.

q: Tisquantum (Squanto), who helped the Pilgrims plant corn, belonged to which Wampanoag band?
fact: He spoke English because he had been kidnapped in 1614 and taken to Europe before making his way home.

q: Thanksgiving's leading advocate, editor Sarah Josepha Hale, also wrote which famous nursery rhyme?
fact: Hale wrote letters to presidents for 17 years asking for a national Thanksgiving before Lincoln agreed.

q: Which Brad Pitt character co-founded the "I Hate Rachel Green Club" in Friends' Thanksgiving episode "The One with the Rumor"?
fact: Pitt was married to Jennifer Aniston (Rachel) when he guest-starred, and he got an Emmy nomination for the role.

q: Norman Rockwell's famous painting of a family about to enjoy a turkey dinner is called…
fact: It was painted in 1943 as part of his Four Freedoms series, inspired by Franklin Roosevelt's 1941 speech.
